_comment: Instrument Tier 3 — 51 control objectives across 14 families, with their accumulation rules. SPEC §3.3/§3.4. Accumulation is expressed as conditions over the SAME engine as routing — there is no second evaluator. Every accumulated objective carries at least one human-readable reason (FR-10). Children fire only on parent Yes, subject to their own cross-tier condition (FR-13).

objectives.name: Unique named accounts
objectives.question: Does everyone who uses this system have their own account, not one shared between people?
objectives.help: A shared account means no action can be traced to a person. If any account is shared — including a vendor's — the honest answer is No or Partial.

accumulated_by.reason: a system holds our data, so every action needs to be traceable to a person
you told us the third party shares one account between people

objectives.name: Privileged credentials vaulted
objectives.question: Are privileged credentials issued from a vault, time-limited, and never held permanently by a person?
objectives.help: A vault issues access when it is needed and takes it back afterwards. Standing administrator passwords, however strong, are not this.

accumulated_by.reason: privileged access is Medium or looser
you told us the third party needs administrator or privileged rights

children.question: For how long is a privileged session valid before it has to be requested again?

objectives.name: Multi-factor authentication
objectives.question: Does signing in require a second factor as well as a password?
objectives.help: For everyone, including vendor staff and break-glass accounts.

accumulated_by.reason: a system holds our data
the system's boundary exposure is Medium or higher

objectives.name: Access recertification
objectives.question: Does somebody periodically confirm that each person still needs the access they hold?
objectives.help: Confirmed by the person accountable for the system or the data, not by the people who hold the access.

accumulated_by.reason: privileged access is Medium or looser
you told us privileged access has never been reviewed, or that you are not sure

objectives.name: Leaver deprovisioning
objectives.question: Is access removed automatically when somebody leaves or changes role?
objectives.help: Automatically means driven by the joiner-leaver process, not by somebody remembering.

accumulated_by.reason: a system holds our data
you told us the third party's leavers come out at a review, or that you are not sure

objectives.name: Third-party access through a controlled gateway
objectives.question: Does the third party reach our systems only through a controlled gateway, rather than directly?
objectives.help: A jump host, a broker, or a zero-trust proxy — something we own that sits between them and the system.

accumulated_by.reason: the third party connects to our systems
you told us they come onto our network over a VPN or private link

objectives.name: Encryption in transit
objectives.question: Is data encrypted every time it moves between components or organisations?
objectives.help: Including internal hops and any file transfer to or from the third party.

accumulated_by.reason: a system stores, processes or transmits our data

objectives.name: Encryption at rest
objectives.question: Is data encrypted where it is stored, including backups?
objectives.help: Backups are the half people forget.

accumulated_by.reason: the most sensitive data involved is Confidential or Restricted
the third party holds our data

objectives.name: Data minimisation
objectives.question: Does this activity collect and pass on only the data it actually needs?
objectives.help: If a whole record is sent where three fields would do, the answer is Partial.

accumulated_by.reason: information about people is involved
the model is given data at the point of use

objectives.name: Key management
objectives.question: Are the encryption keys managed in a key service, with rotation, and held apart from the data?
objectives.help: A key in a configuration file or a repository is not managed.

accumulated_by.reason: Restricted data is involved
the consequence of the third party exposing our data is High

objectives.name: Egress controls
objectives.question: Is there a control that would stop sensitive data leaving through this activity by mistake?
objectives.help: A block or an alert on bulk export, on an unexpected destination, or on sensitive content in an outbound request.

accumulated_by.reason: what the model is given at the point of use is Medium or more exposing
information about people will cross a border

objectives.name: Boundary filtering
objectives.question: Does traffic from the internet pass through something that filters and rate-limits it before it reaches the system?
objectives.help: A web application firewall or an API gateway. A load balancer alone is not this.

accumulated_by.reason: the system is reachable from outside

objectives.name: Segmentation
objectives.question: Is this system separated from the rest of the network, so a compromise here does not reach everything else?
objectives.help: Separate network, separate account, or enforced rules between them — not just a different server.

accumulated_by.reason: boundary exposure is Medium or higher
the third party's reach into our environment is High

objectives.name: Known exposed surface
objectives.question: Is there a current record of exactly what this system exposes to the internet?
objectives.help: Somebody has looked from the outside recently and written down what answers.

accumulated_by.reason: the system is reachable from outside

objectives.name: Authenticated interfaces
objectives.question: Does every interface require authentication, with no unauthenticated endpoint left reachable?
objectives.help: Health checks and documentation pages count as endpoints.

accumulated_by.reason: the system is reachable from outside
partners call it over an API

objectives.name: Central log aggregation
objectives.question: Do access and change logs go somewhere central, outside the reach of the people they record?
objectives.help: If an administrator could delete the log of what they did, the answer is No.

accumulated_by.reason: a system holds our data, so what happens to it has to be recordable

objectives.name: Privileged session recording
objectives.question: Is what a privileged user does recorded, not just the fact that they signed in?
objectives.help: The commands or the changes, not only the login event.

accumulated_by.reason: privileged access is Medium or looser
the third party's reach into our environment is Medium or wider

objectives.name: Log retention
objectives.question: Are logs kept long enough to investigate something discovered months later?
objectives.help: Most obligations land between one and seven years. Days is not enough.

accumulated_by.reason: an incident here would need reconstructing
our ability to reconstruct events is Medium or worse

children.question: For how long?
children.help: As configured today, in months or years.

objectives.name: Alerting on anomalous access
objectives.question: Would anyone be alerted if this system were accessed in an unusual way?
objectives.help: Alerted means a person or a rota receives it, not that it appears in a dashboard nobody opens.

accumulated_by.reason: our ability to reconstruct events is Medium or worse
the activity is critical to the business

objectives.name: Backups held separately
objectives.question: Are backups held somewhere a problem with the system itself could not reach?
objectives.help: A separate account, region or provider — and ideally immutable, so ransomware cannot encrypt them too.

accumulated_by.reason: the business expects this back quickly, or a third party runs something we depend on

objectives.name: Tested restore
objectives.question: Has a restore been performed successfully, end to end, within the last year?
objectives.help: A backup job reporting success is not a tested restore. If nobody has restored it, the answer is No.

accumulated_by.reason: the business expects this back quickly
you told us a restore has not been performed in the last year

children.question: When, and how long did it take?

objectives.name: Documented recovery objectives
objectives.question: Is there an agreed, written recovery time and data-loss tolerance for this activity?
objectives.help: Agreed with the business, not assumed by the technical team.

accumulated_by.reason: you told us the business needs this back within a day
business criticality is Medium or higher

objectives.name: Vendor continuity assurance
objectives.question: Have we seen evidence of the third party's own continuity and recovery arrangements?
objectives.help: Their tested plan or an assurance report — not a clause promising they have one.

accumulated_by.reason: the third party runs something we could not operate without
losing this third party would be felt within days

objectives.name: Named operational owner
objectives.question: Is there a named team accountable for running this once it is live?
objectives.help: A team and a rota, not the name of whoever built it.

accumulated_by.reason: business criticality is Medium or higher

objectives.name: Runbook and support route
objectives.question: Is there a written runbook, and a route by which somebody gets woken up if it breaks?
objectives.help: Written down somewhere a person on call at 3am could find it.

accumulated_by.reason: business criticality is High
you told us the business needs this back within a day

objectives.name: Capacity and performance monitoring
objectives.question: Is somebody watching whether this is keeping up, before users notice it is not?
objectives.help: Monitoring with a threshold that alerts, rather than a graph.

accumulated_by.reason: the activity is used across a business unit or wider

objectives.name: Peer review before release
objectives.question: Does another person review every change before it reaches production?
objectives.help: Reviewed by somebody other than the author, with no route around it.

accumulated_by.reason: changes will be made and released

objectives.name: Automated test gate
objectives.question: Do automated tests have to pass before a change can be released?
objectives.help: Have to, not usually do.

accumulated_by.reason: the path from change to production is Medium or looser

objectives.name: Dependency and secret scanning
objectives.question: Is the code scanned for vulnerable dependencies and for credentials committed by mistake?
objectives.help: On every change, not once at the start.

accumulated_by.reason: changes will be made and released
the system is reachable from outside

objectives.name: Model registered in the inventory
objectives.question: Is this model recorded in the organisation's AI inventory, with a named owner?
objectives.help: The register the AI governance office keeps. If you do not know whether it is there, that is a No — somebody will confirm.

accumulated_by.reason: the activity uses AI

children.question: What is its entry reference?
children.help: The record id or name, as it appears in the inventory.

objectives.name: Model version pinned
objectives.question: Is a specific model version pinned, so it cannot change without us choosing to change it?
objectives.help: If the supplier can update the model under you and you would not know, the answer is No.

accumulated_by.reason: the model comes from outside our organisation
what we know about the model we rely on is Medium or less

objectives.name: Output quality baseline
objectives.question: Is there a measured baseline for how often the output is right, checked before release and after changes?
objectives.help: A number from a test set, not an impression from a demo.

accumulated_by.reason: the AI drafts or classifies something that travels onward
the consequence of a confidently wrong output is Medium or higher

objectives.name: Human review before consequential action
objectives.question: Does a person approve anything the AI does that would affect a customer or a person's outcome?
objectives.help: Approve beforehand. Seeing it afterwards is a different control — that one is logging.

accumulated_by.reason: the AI can act before a person sees what it did
you told us the AI makes a decision without a person in the loop
you told us the AI classifies, scores or ranks people or cases

objectives.name: Ability to disable
objectives.question: Can a person switch this off within minutes, without taking down something else?
objectives.help: A configuration flag somebody on call can set, not a code change and a release.

accumulated_by.reason: the activity uses AI, so somebody has to be able to stop it
the AI acts on its own in ways that reach beyond the team

objectives.name: Prompt and output logging
objectives.question: Is what went into the model and what came out recorded, so a specific answer can be reconstructed later?
objectives.help: Enough to answer 'why did it say that, to whom, and when'.

accumulated_by.reason: the activity uses AI and its behaviour has to be reviewable
the consequence of a wrong output is Medium or higher

objectives.name: Regulatory applicability assessed
objectives.question: Has somebody confirmed which laws and regulations apply to this activity?
objectives.help: Confirmed by legal or compliance, and written down.

accumulated_by.reason: you told us a specific law, regulation or contractual obligation applies

objectives.name: Record of processing
objectives.question: Is this activity recorded in the register of how we process personal information?
objectives.help: The record the privacy office maintains. It is their register, but somebody has to tell them.

accumulated_by.reason: the use is Medium or more intrusive from the person's point of view

objectives.name: Individual rights can be fulfilled
